questions.question_text: All the following are true about likelihood ratios except

options.text: Has no relation to post-test probability
Allow better understanding of a diagnostic test

questions.explanation: Likelihood ratios are unaffected by disease prevalence; they relate sensitivity and specificity to post-test probability.

questions.question_text: Funnel plots are used to detect
questions.explanation: Funnel plots are primarily used in meta-analyses to detect publication bias.

questions.question_text: The type of study design used in this study is
questions.explanation: This is a case-control study comparing cases (hip fractures) with matched controls and assessing prior exposures.

questions.question_text: From the above precis, which of the following statements is the least true:

options.text: The GP practices are likely to have computerised data
The sample is likely to be representative of GP practices in the UK
The General Practice Research Database sample is a random sample from the general population
The data in this database has been found to be accurate
The diagnosis of schizophrenia has been validated

correct_answer.text: The sample is likely to be representative of GP practices in the UK

correct_answers.text: The sample is likely to be representative of GP practices in the UK

questions.explanation: Although GPRD is representative, it is not a random sample; larger, computerised practices are overrepresented.

questions.question_text: From the above precis, what was the most significant predictor of hip fractures?
questions.explanation: Previous falls had the highest adjusted odds ratio (3.79) and was the strongest predictor of hip fractures.

questions.question_text: From the above precis, which of the following predicts more hip fractures:
questions.explanation: Schizophrenia diagnosis had a higher adjusted odds ratio (1.73) compared to inhaled corticosteroids (1.26) or smoking (1.24).

questions.question_text: From the above precis, what can we not deduce from this study?

options.text: A diagnosis of schizophrenia is significantly associated with hip fractures
Antipsychotic use is significantly associated with hip fractures
Inhaled corticosteroids are significantly associated with hip fractures
Being overweight is not associated with hip fractures

questions.explanation: Case-control studies can identify associations but cannot establish causality, so we cannot conclude smoking causes fractures.

questions.question_text: According to this study, the next best step for someone who has had a fall would be to:

options.text: Do a thorough falls risk assessment

correct_answer.text: Do a thorough falls risk assessment

correct_answers.text: Do a thorough falls risk assessment

questions.explanation: Since previous falls was the strongest predictor, a falls risk assessment is the most appropriate intervention.

questions.question_text: If the at-risk elderly population in the UK is 55 million then calculate the number of people who have had hip fractures in one year:
questions.explanation: Annual incidence in GPRD (5% population) was 1,362; extrapolated to 55 million gives ~27,000 hip fractures/year.

questions.question_text: What is the most ideal cut-off point to select patients with bowel cancer for treatment with the new medication which has side effects?
questions.explanation: Cut-off point of 3 balances a high true-positive rate with an acceptably low false-positive rate given treatment risks.

questions.question_text: The plot in this precis is termed as
questions.explanation: A plot of sensitivity (true positive rate) versus 1–specificity (false positive rate) across cut-offs is an ROC curve.

questions.question_text: What is the cut-off point on the new test at which you will have the lowest false positive rate?
questions.explanation: False positive rate equals 1−specificity; the lowest occurs at the cut-off point of 1.

questions.question_text: What is on the Y axis of the graph above (Kaplan–Meier plot for depression risk in smokers vs non-smokers)?

options.text: Time to have a relapse of major depression
Probability of not having major depression

correct_answer.text: Probability of not having major depression

correct_answers.text: Probability of not having major depression

questions.explanation: The Kaplan–Meier survival curve plots the probability of remaining free of the event (not having depression) over time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the above figure (Kaplan–Meier plot)?

options.text: The survival rates are similar for both groups at year 4
All the people in the non-smoking group had not developed depression by year 10
There is a significant difference in the probability of developing depression between groups at year 2
The rates of depression are similar across both groups at year 6
All the people in the smoking group had developed depression by year 10

correct_answer.text: The survival rates are similar for both groups at year 4

correct_answers.text: The survival rates are similar for both groups at year 4

questions.explanation: At year 4 the curves overlap, indicating similar probabilities of remaining depression-free at that time point.

questions.question_text: The following can be deduced from the above graph (Kaplan–Meier plot):

options.text: At year 4, the probability of developing depression is higher in the smoking group compared to non-smoking group
At 10th year, the probability of survival is greater for non-smokers compared to smokers
At 10th year the people in the smoking group had a 100% probability of developing depression
At year 7, the probability of developing depression is higher in the smoking group compared to non-smoking group
At 10th year, the probability of survival is greater for smokers compared to non-smokers

correct_answer.text: At 10th year, the probability of survival is greater for non-smokers compared to smokers

correct_answers.text: At 10th year, the probability of survival is greater for non-smokers compared to smokers

questions.explanation: By year 10 the non-smoking group curve remains above the smoking group, indicating a higher probability of remaining depression-free in non-smokers.

questions.question_text: Select the Male:Female ratios in the following conditions: Attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder; Autism; Bulimia.
questions.explanation: ADHD M:F ≈3:1 (F), Autism ≈4:1 (G), Bulimia ≈1:10 (E).

questions.question_text: Choose appropriate treatment for each of the following child & adolescent presentations: (1) A 4-year-old disrespectful to teachers, (2) A 17-year-old aggressive leading to court injunction, (3) A 13-year-old hyperkinetic child.
questions.explanation: Conduct disorder in young child: parent training (G); severe adolescent aggression: risperidone (I); ADHD: methylphenidate (F).

questions.question_text: Select the most appropriate sampling technique for each: (1) participants from only selected areas; (2) recruits from odd-numbered houses; (3) study of people with personality disorders in a therapeutic community.
questions.explanation: Selected areas: cluster sampling (A); odd-numbered houses: systematic sampling (I); purposive qualitative sampling for personality disorder experiences (D).

questions.question_text: Which would be the most ethical design for each research question: (1) Prevalence of cyclothymia in primary care; (2) Mentally ill patients’ perspectives on quality of care; (3) Risk of psychotic disorders in illegal immigrants; (4) Compare new drug vs placebo in clozapine-induced hypersalivation with fewer participants.
questions.explanation: Prevalence: cross-sectional survey (C); patient perspectives: qualitative (I); immigrant risk: cohort study (D); drug vs placebo with fewer subjects: crossover RCT (B).

questions.question_text: From a study screening terminally ill patients for depression with a single question and DSM-IV interview, results: Interview+ DSM+ 11; Interview+ DSM– 14; Interview– DSM+ 9; Interview– DSM– 40. Calculate: sensitivity; specificity; positive predictive value; proportion of depressed who screened positive; negative predictive value.
questions.explanation: Sensitivity=11/20=55%; Specificity=40/54≈74%; PPV=11/25=44%; proportion depressed screened+ =55%; NPV=40/49≈82%.

questions.question_text: From a systematic review of continuing antidepressants: control event rate (placebo), experimental event rate (SSRI), absolute benefit increase, NNT for MAO-I, NNT for all antidepressants.

Choose the personality disorder for each scenario: (1) 40-year-old hostile toward colleagues, suspicious of infidelity; (2) 40-year-old stockbroker grandiose, upset at perceived slights; (3) 24-year-old with unstable relationships, self-harm threats.
questions.explanation: Hostile suspicion = Paranoid (H); grandiosity = Narcissistic (G); unstable relationships & self-harm = Borderline (E).

questions.question_text: Match statistical terms: (1) Probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis; (2) Probability of finding a difference if it exists; (3) Range within which true value lies 19 out of 20 times; (4) Probability of accepting a false null hypothesis; (5) Probability of observed result given null hypothesis true.
questions.explanation: Type I error = α; Power = 1–β; 95% CI; Type II error = β; p value = probability under null hypothesis.

questions.question_text: For reversible dementia causes, choose the treatment: (1) 55-year-old with memory disturbance, morning headache, facial nerve palsy; (2) 60-year-old with memory problems, ataxia, nystagmus, asterixis; (3) 65-year-old with cognitive impairment, incontinence, ataxia.
questions.explanation: Brain tumour: surgical evacuation (E); Wernicke’s encephalopathy: thiamine (G); normal pressure hydrocephalus: shunt (F).

questions.question_text: For each neuropsychiatric presentation choose the diagnosis: (1) 62-year-old with falls, shuffling gait, vertical gaze palsy; (2) 15-year-old with halting gait post-sore throat; (3) 40-year-old with memory loss, clumsiness, jerky muscle movements.
questions.explanation: Falls & vertical gaze palsy = PSP (H); post-streptococcal chorea = Sydenham’s chorea (I); rapid dementia & myoclonus = CJD (A).

questions.question_text: Choose the type of validity for each instrument description: (1) Paranoid PD patients score higher on MMPI paranoid scale; (2) New panic scale correlates with validated scale; (3) New self-harm scale predicts repeat self-harm at 6 months; (4) New GAD questionnaire covers all cognitive, behavioural, biological symptoms.
questions.explanation: MMPI comparison = criterion validity (D); concurrent correlation = concurrent validity (A); future prediction = predictive validity (G); comprehensive symptom coverage = content validity (C).

questions.question_text: Two curative factors in group therapy are:
questions.explanation: Yalom’s curative factors include group cohesiveness (A) and universality (I) among others.

questions.question_text: For each substance presentation, choose the diagnosis: (1) 18-year-old with visual hallucinations, dilated pupils, increased appetite; (2) 24-year-old with dilated pupils, reduced appetite, auditory hallucinations, insomnia, irritability; (3) 34-year-old with slurred speech, incoordination, nystagmus.
questions.explanation: Cannabis intoxication (E); amphetamine intoxication (C); acute alcohol or benzodiazepine intoxication (A/D) present with incoordination, slurred speech, nystagmus.

questions.question_text: Attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (Male:Female ratio)
questions.explanation: ADHD is more common in males at a ratio of 3:1 in community samples (and up to 9:1 in clinic samples).

questions.question_text: Autism (Male:Female ratio)
questions.explanation: A large review of prevalence studies found the M:F ratio for autism is around 3.8:1, approximated as 4:1.

questions.question_text: Bulimia (Male:Female ratio)
questions.explanation: Bulimia is more common in females; occurrence in males is about one-tenth that in females (1:10).

questions.question_text: A 4 year old child, disrespectful to teachers and hence banned from nursery – treatment
questions.explanation: NICE recommends group-based parent-training/education programmes in the management of children with conduct disorders.

questions.question_text: A 17 year old, aggressive in all circumstances with a court injunction – treatment
questions.explanation: Risperidone is the most widely prescribed drug for conduct disorder in extreme cases, though it is not licensed for CD.

questions.question_text: A 13 year old girl, aggressive, in trouble at school, diagnosed as hyperkinetic – treatment
questions.explanation: NICE recommends methylphenidate as the first-line drug for ADHD (hyperkinetic disorder).

questions.question_text: Participants from only selected areas are included – sampling technique
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling divides the population into groups (clusters), randomly selects clusters, and includes all units in selected clusters.

questions.question_text: Participants recruited from odd numbered houses – sampling technique
questions.explanation: Systematic sampling selects participants at regular intervals from a sampling frame, giving each unit an equal probability.

questions.question_text: Experiences of people with personality disorders in therapeutic community – sampling technique
questions.explanation: Qualitative studies typically use purposive sampling to select participants with specific experiences.

questions.question_text: Prevalence of cyclothymia in primary care attendees – most ethical design
questions.explanation: A cross-sectional survey provides a 'snapshot' of prevalence and characteristics at one point in time.

questions.question_text: Mentally ill patients’ perspectives on quality of care – most ethical design
questions.explanation: Qualitative methods interpret phenomena in terms of meanings people bring, ideal for patient perspectives.

questions.question_text: Risk of psychotic disorders in illegal immigrants in the UK – most ethical design
questions.explanation: A cohort study follows exposed and unexposed groups over time to assess risk of psychosis.

questions.question_text: Compare new drug for clozapine-induced hypersalivation vs placebo with fewer participants – design
questions.explanation: A cross-over trial has each participant receive both interventions sequentially, increasing power with fewer subjects.

questions.question_text: What was the sensitivity of the screening test?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity = a/(a+c) = 11/20 = 55%.

questions.question_text: What was the specificity of the screening test?
questions.explanation: Specificity = d/(b+d) = 40/54 ≈ 74%.

questions.question_text: What was the positive predictive value of the test?
What proportion of those who were depressed screened positive?
questions.explanation: This is sensitivity again: 44%.

questions.question_text: What was the negative predictive value?
Control event rate in the placebo group
Experimental event rate in the SSRI group
Overall absolute benefit increase
Number needed to treat for the MAO-I group
Number needed to treat for the Antidepressant group
40 year old man, hostile, unfounded suspicions of colleagues and spouses – personality disorder
questions.explanation: Paranoid Personality Disorder features unfounded suspicions, hostility, grudges, and doubts about spouse fidelity.

questions.question_text: 40 year old stock broker, grandiose, insults staff, drinks due to lack of appreciation – personality disorder
questions.explanation: Narcissistic PD is characterized by inflated self-importance, need for admiration, and sensitivity to criticism.

questions.question_text: 24 year old woman, unstable relationships, self-harm threats, suicidal gestures – personality disorder
questions.explanation: Emotionally unstable (borderline) PD features impulsivity, unstable relationships, chronic emptiness, and self-destructive behavior.

questions.question_text: The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true
questions.explanation: Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis (false positive).

questions.question_text: The probability of finding a difference if it existed
questions.explanation: Power is the probability that a test will reject a false null hypothesis (1 – β).

questions.question_text: The range within which the true difference value lies 19 out of 20 times
questions.explanation: A 95% confidence interval gives the range likely to contain the true parameter in 19 of 20 samples.

questions.question_text: A probability of accepting a false null hypothesis
questions.explanation: Type II error is accepting a false null hypothesis (false negative).

questions.question_text: The probabilities of observing the study result in a random sample, given that the null hypothesis is true
questions.explanation: The p-value is the probability of observing the data (or more extreme) under the null hypothesis.

questions.question_text: 55 year old lady with memory disturbance and early morning headaches that improve, facial nerve palsy – treatment
questions.explanation: Early morning headache and focal sign suggest a brain tumor; surgical evacuation is indicated.

questions.question_text: 60 year old lady with memory problems, ataxia, nystagmus and asterixis – treatment
questions.explanation: This presentation suggests Wernicke's encephalopathy (alcoholic), treated with thiamine.

questions.question_text: 65 year old lady with mild cognitive impairment, urinary incontinence and ataxia – treatment
questions.explanation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus triad (incontinence, gait, cognition) is treated with a surgical shunt.

questions.question_text: 62 year old lady with frequent falls, wide-based shuffling gait, vertical gaze palsy and micrographia – diagnosis
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy causes supranuclear gaze palsy, parkinsonism, gait disturbance, and falls.

questions.question_text: 15 year old girl with halting gait, difficulty writing, uncoordinated limbs after fever and sore throat – diagnosis
questions.explanation: Sydenham chorea follows streptococcal infection and causes involuntary movements and uncoordinated gait.

questions.question_text: 40 year old man with gait instability, clumsiness, jerky movements and memory loss – diagnosis
questions.explanation: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease presents with rapid dementia, clumsiness, jerky movements, and myoclonus.

questions.question_text: Paranoid PD patients score much higher on a paranoid subscale than normals – validity type
questions.explanation: Criterion validity is demonstrated by comparing a measure with a gold standard or validated instrument.

questions.question_text: New Panic Disorder scale scores highly correlate with older validated scale – validity type
questions.explanation: Concurrent validity is the agreement with another scale that has been shown to be valid.

questions.question_text: After self-harm, ADSH scores predict further self-harm over 6 months – validity type
questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the agreement between a measurement now and outcomes in the future.

questions.question_text: AGAD questionnaire covers cognitive, metacognitive, behavioral and biological symptoms – validity type
questions.explanation: Content validity refers to the extent that a scale covers all important aspects of the construct.

questions.question_text: Two curative factors in group therapy
questions.explanation: Yalom’s curative factors include cohesiveness (belonging) and universality (shared problems among members).

questions.question_text: Three factors that hinder working in groups
questions.explanation: Bion described basic assumptions that hinder groups: dependence, fight-flight, and pairing.

questions.question_text: Two factors found in psychodynamic groups
questions.explanation: Psychodynamic groups use free-floating discussion (group-analytic free association) and interpreting transference.

questions.question_text: 18 year old man with vivid visual hallucinations, dilated pupils, increased appetite – substance diagnosis
questions.explanation: Cannabis intoxication causes euphoria, relaxation, hallucinations, increased appetite, and dilated pupils.

questions.question_text: 24 year old man with dilated pupils, reduced appetite, auditory hallucinations, insomnia and irritability – substance diagnosis
questions.explanation: Amphetamine intoxication presents with dilated pupils, insomnia, loss of appetite, irritability, and hallucinations.

questions.question_text: 34 year old man with slurred speech, incoordination of movements, and nystagmus – substance diagnosis
questions.explanation: Acute alcohol and benzodiazepine intoxication both cause slurred speech, incoordination, and nystagmus.

questions.question_text: The percentage of people in western Europe with a diagnosis of schizophrenia being treated in the community, who smoke is?
questions.explanation: Approximately 60–90% of patients with schizophrenia smoke, compared to about 25% in the general population.

questions.question_text: The following should be in the differential diagnosis for NMS
questions.explanation: NMS can mimic encephalitis, toxic encephalopathy, malignant hyperthermia, among others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for NMS?
questions.explanation: Risk factors include younger age, male gender, and depot (long-acting) antipsychotic formulations.

questions.question_text: You are using a motivational interview approach on a patient with hypochondriasis. Which of the following should be used?

options.text: Making the patient feel that you understand them
Making the patient feel that you believe them
Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change

correct_answer.text: Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change

correct_answers.text: Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change

questions.explanation: Motivational interviewing focuses on exploring and amplifying ambivalence rather than direct persuasion or confrontation.

questions.question_text: The risk of suicide after 1 year of self-harming is
questions.explanation: Systematic review data indicate a 0.5–2% risk of completed suicide within one year following deliberate self-harm.

questions.question_text: To diagnose substance dependence by ICD-10, how many criteria must be met?
questions.explanation: ICD-10 requires three or more of the dependence criteria be present within the past year.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old appears to be experiencing symptoms of diazepam withdrawal. The following is not seen:
questions.explanation: Diazepam withdrawal causes hypotension and tachycardia rather than hypertension.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man presents with pseudohallucinations and quasi-psychotic symptoms, appearing eccentric and withdrawn. Most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Schizotypal personality disorder features odd beliefs and under stress may decompensate to transient psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man with schizophrenia asks about the percentage who discontinue medication during the first year of treatment. The rate is approximately:
questions.explanation: About 26% of first-episode schizophrenia patients stop antipsychotic medication within the first year.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is recommended in the treatment of an adolescent girl with hypomania?
questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics such as olanzapine are recommended first-line in adolescent hypomania to avoid teratogenic risks.

questions.question_text: Which type of memory is most likely to be damaged in Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome?
questions.explanation: Episodic memory (the ability to recall personal events) is most severely affected in amnestic syndromes.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old breastfeeding woman with hypomania. The best treatment option is:
questions.explanation: Most antipsychotics (excluding clozapine) are considered safer in breastfeeding than mood stabilizers like lithium or valproate.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old man with simple schizophrenia. Which is NOT a feature of simple schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Simple schizophrenia is characterized by negative symptoms without overt delusions or hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an actuarial risk assessment instrument for sexual offending?
questions.explanation: The Sex Offender Risk Appraisal Guide (SORAG) is an actuarial tool for predicting sexual recidivism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would you find in Prader–Willi syndrome?
questions.explanation: Skin picking occurs in up to 70% of individuals with Prader–Willi syndrome.

questions.question_text: When assessing a patient with early dementia, which finding suggests a subcortical rather than cortical cause?
questions.explanation: Calculation ability is typically preserved until late in subcortical dementias.

questions.question_text: The following is a measure of internal validity:
questions.explanation: Reliability (accuracy and consistency of measures) reflects internal validity of an instrument.

questions.question_text: What treatment would you use for a patient with severe symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome?
questions.explanation: SSRIs, such as fluoxetine, have the strongest evidence for efficacy in severe PMS.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old boy with intrusive contamination thoughts and rituals. Which medication is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Sertraline is licensed for OCD in children and adolescents.

questions.question_text: A young man with alcoholic relatives asks his increased risk of alcohol dependence. It is approximately:
questions.explanation: Having a first-degree relative with alcohol dependence doubles the risk (~2-fold).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of nominal data?
questions.explanation: Gender is a categorical variable without inherent order and is thus nominal data.

questions.question_text: According to Kernberg the psychodynamic understanding of borderline personality disorder did not include
questions.explanation: The intrapsychic features pointed by Kernberg included partially intact reality testing, that is vulnerable to alterations and failures because of aggression.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding pharmacokinetics in the elderly

options.text: No change in renal function with age
No change in hepatic function with age

questions.explanation: In older people there is gradual reduction in renal & hepatic function with increase in body fat hence leading to increased distribution of psychotropics.

questions.question_text: In a positive skew graph, which of the following is true

options.text: Mean is equal to median & mode

questions.explanation: The mean is higher than the median in positively (right) skewed distributions and lower than the median in negatively (left) skewed distributions.

questions.question_text: The following would suggest severe lithium toxicity
questions.explanation: Severe lithium intoxication occurs at levels > than 2.5 meq /L and can cause generalised convulsions, oliguria, renal failure and death. More moderate lithium intoxication causes nausea, blurred vision, nystagmus and hyperreflexia.

questions.question_text: Tolerance doesn't or is less likely to develop in the following in opiate dependence syndrome
questions.explanation: Tolerance to miosis occurs at a much slower rate.

questions.question_text: Which method of randomisation should be avoided
questions.explanation: By assigning patients with odd/even number dates the two groups might differ significantly affecting the results. To avoid this treatments should be assigned randomly.

questions.question_text: A mother asks you what is the chances of her 12 year old son with conduct disorder going on to develop antisocial personality disorder
questions.explanation: A study conducted on a nationally representative sample (NESARC) found that approximately 75% of those with Conduct disorder also met criteria for Antisocial personality disorder, contradicting previous views that only about 40% go on to have ASPD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the characteristic feature in transient global amnesia

options.text: Transient loss of short term memory
Retained ability to retain new Information

correct_answer.text: Transient loss of short term memory

correct_answers.text: Transient loss of short term memory

questions.explanation: Transient global amnesia manifests with a paroxysmal, transient loss of memory function. Immediate recall ability is preserved, as is remote memory; however, patients experience striking loss of memory for recent events and an impaired ability to retain new information.

questions.question_text: The most common delusion associated with stalking is
questions.explanation: The delusional conviction of being loved by someone who is identified but unattainable is the basis of erotomania or de Clerambault's syndrome, which forms the majority of the sample of stalkers.

questions.question_text: In the following series of numbers 1, 2, 3, 7, 2, 5 the following is correct

options.text: cannot comment on mean, median or mode

questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value (2). The median is 2.5 and the mean is 3.33.

questions.question_text: A patient who has recently completed an inpatient detoxification from opiates would like to be prescribed something that will help to prevent relapse. Which of the following would be the most appropriate
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine and methadone are first-line maintenance treatments of opiate dependence. Naltrexone is used in maintenance treatment specifically to prevent relapse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not metabolised by CYP2D6?
questions.explanation: The noradrenaline-selective antidepressant reboxetine in vitro is a weak inhibitor of both cytochrome P450 (CYP) 2D6 and CYP3A4. Kuhn et al (2007) Reboxetine and cytochrome P450—comparison with paroxetine treatment in humans. Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther. 45(1):36-46. & Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1085.

questions.question_text: Autism is most likely to be associated with which of the following:
questions.explanation: Hyperactivity is common with autism. Goodman & Scott, Child Psychiatry, 2002, pg 43.

questions.question_text: The following could commonly lead to oral contraceptive failure
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is a potent inducer of hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes and is metabolised by CYP3A4. Patients receiving contraception should either receive a preparation containing less than 50 micrograms of oestrogen or use a non-hormonal method. Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 2009, 9th edn, pg 136.

questions.question_text: Apperceptive agnosia is the inability to
questions.explanation: Apperceptive agnosics cannot copy objects or drawings unless they do so lavishly and very slowly, often producing frequent errors. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 64.

questions.question_text: A 40 year-old man who is a heavy drinker does not recognise that he requires to change and does not accept his problem drinking. Regarding his motivation to change he is in the stage of
questions.explanation: At the precontemplation stage there is no intention to change and patients are not even aware of their problem. Secret drinking is seen in this stage. Handbook of Alcoholism, 2000, Zernig et al, pg 99–100.

questions.question_text: The following is commonly seen in a patient with anorexia nervosa
questions.explanation: In a community sample of 214 women with anorexia nervosa, common findings included anemia 38.6%, leukocytopenia 34.4%, hyponatremia 19.7%, hypokalemia 19.7%, bradycardia 41.3%, hypotension 16.1%, hypothermia 22.4%, elevated ALT 12.2%, osteopenia 51.7%, osteoporosis 34.6%, primary amenorrhea 14.8%. Miller et al. Arch Intern Med. 2005;165:561–566.

questions.question_text: In interpersonal therapy, which is the most appropriate stance for the therapist to take?

options.text: To act as the patient's advocate

correct_answer.text: To act as the patient's advocate

correct_answers.text: To act as the patient's advocate

questions.explanation: The therapeutic role of a therapist in IPT is to be a patient's advocate (not neutral), be active (not passive), the therapeutic relationship is not interpreted as transference and is not a friendship. Klerman, Interpersonal Therapy for Depression, Basic Books, 1984, pg 73–76.

questions.question_text: Common side effects of Cyproterone acetate include
questions.explanation: The commonest side effects (affecting 1 in 10) include decreased libido, reduced sperm production, impotence and reduced volume of sperm.

questions.question_text: The most common side effect of Rivastigmine is
questions.explanation: The most common adverse effects associated with Rivastigmine are nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, anorexia, fatigue, and somnolence. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1034.

questions.question_text: In PANSS which of the following is considered to be a positive symptom?
questions.explanation: The items on the positive scale include Delusions, Conceptual disorganization, Hallucinatory behavior, Excitement, Grandiosity, Suspiciousness and Hostility. Kay et al. Schizophrenia Bulletin 13(2):261–276.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely diagnosis that an in-patient with HIV is most likely to have?
questions.explanation: The commonest CNS manifestation in patients with HIV disease has emerged as HIV-associated dementia. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 408.

questions.question_text: In autism the following is true

options.text: Perinatal complications not associated with autism
Not associated with Fragile X syndrome
Rates have been found to be higher in patients exposed to the MMR vaccine

questions.explanation: Early twin studies estimated the heritability of autism to be more than 90%. Monozygotic concordance is >90%. Autism is seen in around 25% of male patients with fragile X and 6% of females. Perinatal complications are associated but may not be causal. Rutter (2000); Abrahams & Geschwind (2008).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is recognised to cause schizophrenia-like psychosis?
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease can present with florid schizophrenic symptoms and may appear before the true diagnosis becomes apparent. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 580.

questions.question_text: A journalist asks about the probability of an offender released from medium-secure units going on to commit a further offence?
questions.explanation: Although reoffending rates vary from 7% to 50%, data from England and Wales show rates around 7%. Max Rutherford & Sean Duggan. Forensic Practice, 10(4), 2008, 4–10.

questions.question_text: In an RCT 50 patients are allocated placebo and 50 to treatment. However 6 patients refuse the active treatment. Which is true?

options.text: Analyse refusers as a separate group
Include refusers in the treatment arm during analysis
Include refusers in the placebo arm during analysis

correct_answer.text: Include refusers in the treatment arm during analysis

correct_answers.text: Include refusers in the treatment arm during analysis

questions.explanation: Results should usually be reported on an intention-to-treat (ITT) basis: everyone randomized to a group is analysed in that group. Common ITT methods include last observation carried forward, worst-case scenarios, and mean imputation.

questions.question_text: Smoking does not affect the metabolism of which of the following medications?
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke induces CYP1A2, reducing plasma levels of many psychotropics. Lithium is excreted by the kidneys and is not metabolised. Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 2009, pg 492–493.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common neurological side effect of fluoxetine?
questions.explanation: Common adverse effects of fluoxetine include nervousness, anxiety, headache, insomnia, dizziness and tremor. BNF, 2009, pg 213.

questions.question_text: A patient is seen with yawning, dysphoria and dilated pupils. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Amphetamine intoxication can cause pupillary dilation, dysphoria and yawning, along with cardiovascular risks. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 410.

questions.question_text: A drug is considered teratogenic if it raises birth abnormalities above expected prevalence. What is that prevalence?
questions.explanation: The UK Teratology Information Service suggests the average risk of congenital abnormalities is 2-3%; lithium in pregnancy increases it to about 10%. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 750.

questions.question_text: Which personality disorder is most common in patients over 60 who commit suicide?
questions.explanation: In older suicides, personality disorder or trait accentuation was present in 44%, most frequently anankastic or anxious traits. Harwood et al. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry. 2001;16(2):155–165.

questions.question_text: Patient experienced lithium toxicity: all the following increase risk except
questions.explanation: Drugs that increase lithium toxicity include ACE inhibitors, diuretics, NSAIDs, carbamazepine and SSRIs. Aminophylline does not. Maudsley Guidelines, 2009, pg 132–133.

questions.question_text: The following is a feature of Progressive supranuclear palsy:

options.text: Lateral gaze problems are an early feature

questions.explanation: In PSP onset is usually in the 6th decade; ocular symptoms affect vertical gaze; frequent backward (often forward-predominant) falls occur; neurofibrillary tangles are in basal ganglia, brainstem and cerebellar nuclei. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 776.

questions.question_text: The ideal value for κ (kappa) is
questions.explanation: Kappa measures inter-rater reliability. If raters are in complete agreement then κ=1; if agreement is only that expected by chance, κ=0. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 189.

questions.question_text: A mother asks which category of schizophrenia has the 'best' prognosis:
questions.explanation: Hebephrenic and catatonic forms tend to have the worst prognosis; the paranoid form has the best. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 397.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is adjusted for the age of the population?
questions.explanation: The Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) is an indirect age-adjusted measure comparing observed to expected deaths if the study population had the mortality experience of a standard population. Gordis, Epidemiology, 3rd edn, pp 64–65.

questions.question_text: One of the following statements is less accurate than the others:

options.text: Unilateral ECT causes more memory problems than bilateral ECT

correct_answer.text: Unilateral ECT causes more memory problems than bilateral ECT

correct_answers.text: Unilateral ECT causes more memory problems than bilateral ECT

questions.explanation: Bilateral ECT (not unilateral) has been associated with a higher incidence of memory problems. NICE guidelines for ECT, 2003.

questions.question_text: An infarct in which region leads to an increased rate of depression:
questions.explanation: MRI-documented infarcts in hippocampus, basal ganglia and frontal areas have been classically associated with post-stroke depression. Frodl et al. J Clin Psychiatry. 2004;65:492–499.

questions.question_text: Which of the below increases the power of a study:

options.text: Comparing active treatment vs active treatment
A scale with a lot of subscales

questions.explanation: Power depends on sample size, effect size, reliability of measures and alpha. Effect size is maximized when comparing an active treatment to placebo (no treatment).

questions.question_text: Smoking in a pregnant lady can lead to the following in the child
questions.explanation: Smoking in pregnancy is associated with ADHD and behaviour problems including conduct disorders and antisocial behaviour in the child. Langley et al. BMC Psychiatry. 2007;7:26.

questions.question_text: An anorexic patient presents with shortness of breath and fainting episodes. Which would account for this?
questions.explanation: Anaemia is a common haematological finding in anorexia and can manifest with shortness of breath and fainting spells. Oxford Handbook of Clinical Medicine, 7th edn, pg 310.

questions.question_text: A woman lost her mother recently. A feature which would take your diagnosis towards depression rather than normal grief reaction:
questions.explanation: Symptoms of retardation and global loss of self-esteem are seldom present in uncomplicated grief. Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th edn, pg 170.

questions.question_text: A 16 year-old boy is found drunk in school just before a presentation. He has stopped going out with friends and refuses family meals. Most likely diagnosis:
questions.explanation: Social phobia is a persistent fear of social situations with embarrassment, which can lead to alcohol misuse. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 470–471.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would you see abnormal language development in?
questions.explanation: Language deficits and difficulty using language to communicate ideas are key criteria for autistic disorder. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1194.

questions.question_text: People with emotionally unstable borderline personality disorder are in:
questions.explanation: According to Kernberg, borderline individuals use splitting and remain in the paranoid-schizoid position. Borderline Personality Disorder, Lubit & Finley-Belgrad.

questions.question_text: The following gives an association of the rate of disease development:
questions.explanation: Incidence (inception) rate refers to the rate of new cases arising. Understanding Clinical Papers, Bowers & Owens, p 89.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding Fragile X?

options.text: IQ is stable in adult patients
Severity depends on the number of CGG repeats

questions.explanation: Cognitive decline is a feature of Fragile X syndrome; IQ declines with age; CGG counts >200 lead to the full mutation. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 549.

questions.question_text: You see a patient with dementia who also has peripheral neuropathy. A tumour in which organ could cause this presentation?
questions.explanation: Cancers of the lung can cause peripheral neuropathies, confusion, cerebellar syndrome and polymyositis. Oxford Handbook of Clinical Medicine, 7th edn, pg 162.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is the most common cause of SIADH?
questions.explanation: SSRIs (particularly citalopram) are most often associated with hyponatraemia and SIADH. Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 2009, pg 193.

questions.question_text: An elderly gentleman has delusional disorder. Which is true about this disorder?

options.text: Older onset is associated with somatic delusions

questions.explanation: Persecutory delusions are the most common subtype (up to 60%) followed by somatic then grandiose. Yamada et al. Acta Psychiatr Scand. 1998;97(2):122–124.

questions.question_text: Containment is best described as the:

options.text: Patient's ability to deal with anger
Patient's ability to deal with unpleasant emotions
Therapist's ability to keep the patient's emotions to himself
Therapist's ability to keep the patient's actions to himself
Therapist's ability to modify and return the patient's difficult material so it can be tolerated

correct_answer.text: Therapist's ability to modify and return the patient's difficult material so it can be tolerated

correct_answers.text: Therapist's ability to modify and return the patient's difficult material so it can be tolerated

questions.explanation: Containment is the therapist's ability to modify and return the patient's difficult emotions in a way the patient can tolerate. Holmes, Textbook of Psychotherapy in Psychiatric Practice, pg 321.

questions.question_text: The most commonly used antidepressant in post-stroke depression is
questions.explanation: More studies show efficacy of fluoxetine in post-stroke depression. Whyte & Mulsant, Biol Psychiatry. 2002;52(3):253–264.

questions.question_text: A patient with Parkinson's disease becomes distressingly psychotic. Which can be used?
questions.explanation: Low-dose clozapine is the only atypical antipsychotic fully recommended for Parkinson's psychosis. The Parkinson Study Group. N Engl J Med. 1999;340(10):757–763.

questions.question_text: A man saw his friend seriously injured in a car he was driving. He now avoids driving that way. Most likely diagnosis:
questions.explanation: Avoidance of reminders of a traumatic event is a core feature of PTSD. Adjustment reactions are less catastrophic. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 477.
